newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-AC MILAN EDGE CLOSER TO CUP QUARTER-FINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AC MILAN EDGE CLOSER TO CUP QUARTER-FINALS.

text.p: AC Milan fought their way closer to a place in the quarter-finals of the European Cup with a tense 1-1 draw against Porto in an ill-tempered Champions' League Group D match on Wednesday.

The draw meant that the Portuguese champions, unbeaten so far in the competition and with one Champions' League game to come, finished first in the group and meet the runners-up of Group C in the last eight.

AC Milan, who were clearly highly nervous at the start, need only a point against Norway's Rosenborg next month to go through, although their reward will be an Italian derby with reigning European champions Juventus.

The tension visible throughout the closely-fought game apparently erupted into blows after the players left the pitch. Eye-witnesses said Milan's Liberian striker George Weah punched Porto defender Jorge Costa in the tunnel leading to the dressing-rooms.
The witnesses said the clash between the two men triggered a series of scuffles involving virtually all the players until officials stepped in to break it up.
A dazed Costa, bleeding profusely from the nose, was led away for medical attention by Porto officials.
Dutch international Edgar Davids had put Milan ahead after 55 minutes with a sweetly-struck drive from inside the area after Weah rose to nod the ball down into his path.
But Porto, who were in the comfortable position of having already qualified for the last eight, refused to surrender as Milan piled on the pressure.
Brazilian striker Mario Jardel, two-goal executioner of Milan in Porto's 3-2 win at the San Siro stadium in September, fell in the penalty area after a tussle with veteran defender Franco Baresi.
Referee Gerd Grabher of Austria spurned the home side's furious demands for a penalty but from the corner which he awarded, Porto got their equaliser.
Brazilian midfielder Edmilson Pimenta fired home after the Milan defence failed to clear the ball in a goalmouth scramble.

Jardel, whose appearance as a substitute early in the second half was greeted with a huge cheer from the 50,000 capacity crowd, nearly got himself on to the score sheet in the 80th minute when he threw himself at a cross from the left by Antonio Folha but his header went just wide.
At the other end, Davids could have had a second a few minutes earlier but his shot flew just wide of the post.
Taut nerves led to a series of heavy tackles and two Milan players, Frenchman Marcel Desailly and Stefano Eranio, were booked in the first five minutes of the match.

Neither will be able to play in the crucial December 4 game against Rosenborg in Milan. The French international was lucky not to have been shown the red card in the first half when he made a second crunching tackle from behind.

Porto - 24-Henrique Hilario, 4-Aloisio Alves, 5-Fernando Mendes, 7-Sergio Conceicao, 11-Ljubimko Drulovic (Mario Jardel 55), 14-Artur Oliveira (Joao Manuel Pinto 84), 17-Jose Barroso, 18-Manuel Bino (Antonio Folha 66), 21-Edmilson Pimenta, 22-Jorge Costa, 25-Zlatko Zahovic.

AC Milan - 1-Sebastiano Rossi, 2-Christian Panucci, 3-Paolo Maldini, 6-Franco Baresi, 8-Marcel Desailly (Massimo Ambrosini 81), 11-Alessandro Costacurta, 24-Stefano Eranio (Cristophe Dugarry 88), 20-Zvonimir Boban, 22-Edgar Davids, 9-George Weah, 18-Roberto Baggio (Marco Simone 79).
